item.title: Datacor Integrates Amazon Quick Sight Generative BI into TrackAbout Solution
item.description:
Datacor Integrates Amazon Quick Sight Generative BI into TrackAbout Solution

Datacor has collaborated with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to integrate Amazon Quick Sight into its TrackAbout solution, providing industrial gas and welding distributors with a multi-tenant rental analytics tool featuring interactive dashboards and a natural language search bar.

💡 Why it matters

Previously, rental data was stored within TrackAbout’s operational systems, but extracting insights required going through Datacor’s support team. Customers had to request raw data exports or custom SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) reports, with delivery times ranging from several days to weeks.

🧩 How it works

The solution relies on an automated cross-cloud data pipeline that ingests and transforms operational data from TrackAbout’s third-party cloud environment into AWS. This pipeline regularly refreshes datasets in Amazon Quick Sight SPICE (Super-fast, Parallel In-memory Calculation Engine) on a scheduled basis to ensure dashboards reflect recent data.

⚙️ Key details

At the center of the experience is Amazon Q in Quick Sight, a generative AI-powered assistant for business intelligence. This capability allows business users to ask plain-language questions and receive contextually relevant answers.

Example Natural Language Queries:

  • “Show me rental revenue by product type last quarter”
  • “Which customers have the most unreturned cylinders this month?”
  • “What is the average rental rate by asset class across my top 20 accounts?”
  • “How many cylinders have been out for more than 90 days?”

Pre-built Dashboard Metrics:

  • Fleet utilization rates
  • Billing exception summaries
  • Revenue recovery trends
  • Customer-level asset aging

🔍 Overview

TrackAbout helps distributors manage cylinder and container assets across the supply chain. Collectively, TrackAbout customers manage over 725,000 bills per month and 27.5 million assets.

#Datacor #AWS #AmazonQuickSight #GenerativeBI #SupplyChain

Source: How Datacor built self-service rental analytics with Amazon Quick Sight | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Deploy Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base for Voice Cloning on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
item.description:
Deploy Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base for Voice Cloning on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

The Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base text-to-speech model is now available for deployment to fully managed, real-time inference endpoints via Amazon SageMaker JumpStart.

🔍 Overview

Qwen3-TTS is a publicly available text-to-speech model family developed by the Qwen team at Alibaba Cloud. The model family supports streaming generation for low-latency, interactive scenarios and uses the Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz speech tokenizer. It covers 10 languages:

  • Chinese
  • English
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • German
  • French
  • Russian
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish
  • Italian

⚙️ Key details

The Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base variant specializes in voice cloning, which reproduces the vocal identity of a specific speaker without retraining.

Model Variant Primary Function
Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base Performs voice cloning from a user-supplied reference audio clip and transcript
Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice Generates speech from a fixed set of predefined speakers

Capabilities of the Base variant include:

  • Rapid Cloning: Captures timbre, pitch, and cadence from only a few seconds of user audio.
  • Cross-lingual Cloning: Captures a voice from a reference in one language and generates speech in another while preserving vocal identity.

🧩 How it works

Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides the model artifacts and a pre-built serving container, removing the need to write a custom inference handler.

  1. Request: A client sends an HTTP request to the Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint containing target text, base64-encoded reference audio, and the reference audio’s transcript.
  2. Routing: Amazon SageMaker AI routes the request to a vLLM-Omni serving container running on a GPU instance.
  3. Generation: The “talker stage” generates speech tokens from the text and reference voice, and the “code2wav stage” renders them into a waveform.
  4. Output: The container generates 24 kHz audio output, returned to the client in the requested format (such as WAV).

🚀 Availability

Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base is available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart alongside Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice and Qwen3-ASR-1.7B. Using Amazon SageMaker AI, users can manage infrastructure provisioning, health monitoring, and automatic scaling for the real-time endpoint.

#AmazonSageMaker #Qwen3 #TextToSpeech #VoiceCloning #MachineLearning

Source: Deploying real-time personalized speech with Qwen3-TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Sony and Universal Music Group Sue Suno Over v6 Model Training
item.description:
Sony and Universal Music Group Sue Suno Over v6 Model Training

Sony and Universal Music Group (UMG) have filed a lawsuit against Suno, alleging that the company’s new v6 model infringes on their copyrights.

⚖️ Legal Allegations

Sony and UMG, who did not sign licensing agreements with Suno, accuse the company of “model laundering.” The labels argue that:

  • Training a new model on the outputs of an infringing model does not eliminate infringement.
  • Value from copied recordings is passed from infringing models into their outputs, and then into v6.
  • v6 is described in the complaint as “the fruit of the same poisoned tree.”
  • Even models not directly trained on the plaintiffs’ recordings benefit from Suno’s “retained unauthorized copies.”

⚙️ Technical Claims

Sony further alleges that Suno utilized distillation to train v6, claiming it was trained to replicate results from previous “teacher” models created using infringing data. The labels contend that Suno’s models will continue to be built on stolen data unless the company starts from scratch.

🔍 Suno’s Response

Regarding the development of v6, Suno representatives have stated the following:

  • Jack Brody told The Verge it was “trained from the ground up, with a new set of data,” which included “user data.”
  • Suno later confirmed to Engadget that this data includes “creations” from users.

#Suno #Copyright #MusicAI #Lawsuit

Source: Sony and UMG are suing Suno again

item.title: AI Edge Gallery Adds Support for Gemma 4 and On-Device Features
item.description:
AI Edge Gallery Adds Support for Gemma 4 and On-Device Features

AI Edge Gallery is a destination for running open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) directly on mobile hardware. The latest version introduces official support for the Gemma 4 family of models, enabling high-performance Generative AI to run fully offline and private.

🔍 Overview

All model inferences occur directly on the device hardware without requiring internet, which ensures privacy for images, prompts, and sensitive data. The platform utilizes Google AI Edge for core APIs and tools, along with LiteRT for optimized model execution.

⚙️ Key Details

Feature Description
Thinking Mode Allows users to see the model’s step-by-step reasoning process; currently supported by the Gemma 4 family.
Agent Skills Augments capabilities with tools such as interactive maps, Wikipedia for fact-grounding, and visual summary cards.
Multimodal Power Uses the photo gallery or camera to solve visual puzzles, identify objects, or generate detailed descriptions.
Voice Capabilities Real-time transcription and translation of voice recordings into text via on-device models.
Dedicated Workspace Provides granular control over model parameters like top-k and temperature for testing prompts and single-turn use cases.
Model Management Includes the ability to download models from a list, load custom models, and run benchmark tests on specific hardware.

🧩 Specialized Capabilities

Certain tasks are powered by a finetune of FunctionGemma 270m:

  • Offline device controls and automated tasks.
  • An experimental mini-game where natural language is used to harvest and plant a virtual garden.

Users can also load modular skills via GitHub Discussions community contributions or from a URL.

🚀 Availability

  • OS Requirements: Android 12 and up; iOS 17 and up.
  • Installation: Available via the App Store, Google Play, or as an apk from the latest release for users without Google Play access.

#AIEdgeGallery #Gemma4 #OnDeviceAI #LLM #MobileAI

Source: google-ai-edge/gallery

item.title: DeepSeek Reverses Decision to Retire V4 Pro Following Week of Routing Drama
item.description:
DeepSeek Reverses Decision to Retire V4 Pro Following Week of Routing Drama

On September 11, DeepSeek reversed its decision to retire its DeepSeek V4 Pro open-weights model, officially committing to continue serving the model at unchanged billing rates. This decision follows a week of retirement drama starting September 8, where the model was initially put on a retirement path to be replaced by V4.1 Flash. The reversal secures DeepSeek V4 Pro’s position as a key text-only competitor to xAI’s proprietary Grok 4.6 flagship.

🔍 Overview

During the week of September 8, DeepSeek placed V4 Pro on a retirement path. Under the initial plan, starting September 14, requests to deepseek-v4-pro were to be routed to V4.1 Flash and billed at Flash prices until a V4.1 Pro model was shipped.

After delaying the cutoff, DeepSeek completely reversed its decision on September 11. The company has now committed to keep serving V4 Pro with unchanged billing, promising to provide notice if this ever changes. As of September 15, the model remains active with a written promise to stay.

⚙️ Key details

Both Grok 4.6 (released August 12, 2026) and DeepSeek V4 Pro (released August 13, 2026) are strong reasoning models with comparable independent scores. However, they represent entirely different product philosophies and technical capabilities:

Feature Grok 4.6 DeepSeek V4 Pro
Model Type Proprietary flagship MIT open-weights
Pricing (per 1M tokens) $2.00 input / $6.00 output $0.66 / $1.98 off-peak ($1.32 / $3.96 peak)
Intelligence Index Score 44 (Ranked #20 of 200) 36 (Ranked #7 of 113 in class)
Generation Speed ~57 tokens/sec ~81 tokens/sec
Context Window 500K 1M
Input Capabilities Text and image Text-only
Access Method xAI API or partner Download weights or API

Grok 4.6 leads by eight points on the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. The premium price for Grok 4.6 buys access to xAI’s ecosystem, image input capability, and a 500K context served by a company focused entirely on that product.

🚀 Availability

Both models are active and accessible today:

  • Grok 4.6 can be called through xAI’s API or a partner.
  • DeepSeek V4 Pro weights can be downloaded under the MIT license to serve yourself, or called via API.
  • OrcaRouter Integration: Both Grok 4.6 and DeepSeek V4 Pro route through OrcaRouter, allowing developers to call either or both models on a single key with provider list prices passed through at zero markup.

💡 Why it matters

This development highlights a clear split in the frontier AI model market depending on your specific infrastructure needs:

  • For Multimodal and Ecosystem-Locked Workloads: If you want a frontier reasoning model with image input, a long context, and no interest in running your own weights, Grok 4.6’s $2/$6 pricing represents fair value for its competitive index rank of 44.
  • For Text-Only, Token-Heavy Workloads: DeepSeek V4 Pro is the highly optimized alternative for nearly every billing-related metric. It is roughly three times cheaper at peak, offers a deeper cache discount, delivers faster output, provides twice the context window, and gives you open weights as an escape hatch. Having survived its brief retirement path, it remains the open-weights option with a written promise to stay.

#DeepSeek #xAI #Grok #OpenWeights #AIModels

Source: DeepSeek V4 Pro vs Grok 4.6: The Price War, Re-Run

item.title: AI Edge Gallery adds support for Gemma 4 and Thinking Mode
item.description:
AI Edge Gallery adds support for Gemma 4 and Thinking Mode

The AI Edge Gallery has been updated to provide official support for the newly released Gemma 4 family of models, enabling users to run powerful open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) locally on mobile devices.

🔍 Overview

AI Edge Gallery is a flexible sandbox and destination for running open-source LLMs directly on hardware. All model inferences happen on-device, meaning no internet is required, ensuring privacy for prompts, images, and sensitive data.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Thinking Mode Allows users to see a model’s step-by-step reasoning process; currently works with supported models starting with Gemma 4.
Agent Skills Augments capabilities with tools like Wikipedia for fact-grounding, interactive maps, and visual summary cards.
Dedicated Workspace A space to test prompts and single-turn use cases with control over temperature and top-k parameters.
Model Management Allows users to download models from a list, load custom models, and run benchmark tests on specific hardware.

🧩 How it works

Users can access various on-device ML/GenAI use cases, including:

  • Multimodal Capabilities: Identifying objects, solving visual puzzles, or getting descriptions via the camera or photo gallery.
  • Audio Processing: Real-time transcription and translation of voice recordings into text.
  • Automated Tasks: Offline device controls and a virtual garden mini-game powered by a finetune of FunctionGemma 270m.
  • Modular Skills: Loading skills via URL or browsing community contributions on GitHub Discussions.

🚀 Availability

  • OS Requirements: Android 12 and up, and iOS 17 and up.
  • Installation: Available via Google Play, App Store, or as an apk from the latest release for users without Google Play access.
  • Technical Foundation: Powered by Google AI Edge (Core APIs and tools) and LiteRT (lightweight runtime for optimized execution).

item.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra Now Generally Available on Amazon Bedrock
item.description:
OpenAI GPT-6 Astra Now Generally Available on Amazon Bedrock

OpenAI has announced the general availability of GPT-6 Astra, its most capable model to date, on the Amazon Bedrock inference engine.

🔍 Overview

GPT-6 Astra is designed for demanding tasks that require greater depth and judgment. It is built to enhance the capabilities of AI agents that automate complex workflows, analyze data, and write code at production scale.

💡 Why it matters

The model applies deeper reasoning to complex business decisions and produces professional-quality output aligned with organizational standards, templates, and voice. Key application examples include:

Use Case Capability
Financial Analysis Reconciles conflicting data sources and identifies discrepancies that could alter recommendations.
Contract Review Reviews hundreds of pages with a context window of up to 1 million input tokens to identify high-risk provisions.
Codebase Management Investigates problems across large codebases, reasons through dependencies, and handles fixes from diagnosis through testing.

⚙️ Key details

  • Interface Capabilities: Advances computer and browser use, allowing the model to work across applications via software interfaces when connectors or APIs are unavailable.
  • Enterprise Integration: New enterprise plugins for ChatGPT Work extend browser-use capabilities across common business applications.
  • Prompt Caching: Supports both implicit and explicit prompt caching for workflows that reuse the same context, such as recurring document reviews. Explicit caching allows users to set cache breakpoints to reduce latency, cost, and repeated processing.

🛡️ Security and Governance

GPT-6 Astra is the first OpenAI model to reach a “Critical” classification for cybersecurity capability under the Preparedness Framework. Security measures include:

  • Real-time Safeguards: Automated safeguards monitor for misuse and can pause or stop activity that exceeds defined boundaries within the Amazon Bedrock service boundary.
  • Infrastructure Protection: Zero-operator access is enforced at the chip level, preventing AWS operators from accessing prompts and completions during inference.
  • Data Security: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit, complemented by AWS controls for auditing model invocation and governing access.

🚀 Availability

Users can access GPT-6 Astra through the following methods:

  • Direct calls via Amazon Bedrock APIs.
  • Configuration of Codex or ChatGPT Work to use the model on Amazon Bedrock.

#OpenAI #AmazonBedrock #GPT6Astra #AIAgents #EnterpriseAI

Source: Take on your most ambitious work with GPT-6 Astra on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Sketch Feature
item.description:
OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Sketch Feature

OpenAI announced ChatGPT Images 2.5 on Tuesday, introducing updated image generation tools and a new feature called Sketch that allows users to use doodles as part of their prompts.

🧩 How it works

Users can now influence image generation through drawing and direct feedback:

  • Sketch: By typing @Sketch into the chat box, a window appears where users can draw a doodle and then tell ChatGPT how to make an image based on that sketch.
  • Direct Comments: Users can leave comments directly on specific parts of images to request changes, such as changing a cat’s eyes from blue to green.

⚙️ Key details

OpenAI stated that ChatGPT Images 2.5 provides several improvements over Images 2.0:

Feature Improvement
Visual Quality More natural lighting and richer textures
Instruction Following Better at following editing instructions across multiple turns
Performance Latency reduced by up to 50% compared with Images 2.0

🚀 Availability

ChatGPT Images 2.5 is currently available for the following users on desktop, mobile, and web:

  • ChatGPT users
  • ChatGPT Work users
  • Codex users

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #AIimages #ImageGeneration

Source: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images

item.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra with Advanced Computer Use and Graphical Capabilities
item.description:
OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra with Advanced Computer Use and Graphical Capabilities

OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, a new model that significantly improves upon its predecessor, GPT-5.6, across multiple categories. While the model shows progress in writing, math, and coding, it is particularly distinguished by its graphical capabilities and its ability to interact with local computer interfaces.

🔍 Overview

GPT-6 Astra represents a major step forward, outperforming the previous GPT-5.6 model in nearly all evaluated areas. It is particularly noted for:

  • Leapfrogging GPT-5.6 in math, coding, and writing.
  • Exceptional performance in image and rendering tasks.
  • The ability to operate local software through the Codex/ChatGPT app.

⚙️ Key details

Independent evaluations from Artificial Analysis provide a look at the model’s performance relative to existing benchmarks. GPT-6 Astra achieved a 99.9% score on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, which measures logic puzzles and generalization, while its predecessor GPT-5.6 Sol reached 7.8%.

Benchmark or Index Details
ARC-AGI-3 Measures logic puzzles and generalization; Astra achieved 99.9%.
Coding Agent Index v1.4 A blend of agentic coding tasks where Astra is currently at the frontier.
Intelligence Index v4.2 A general index blending various task types, including Terminal-Bench v2.1.
Computer Use A capability where the model interacts with GUIs via the mouse cursor on local machines.

🧩 How it works

Evaluation accuracy depends on the specific harness used during testing. While models are often optimized for a primary harness during training, independent benchmarks use various setups to provide more trustworthy results:

  • Stirrup: An open-source, minimal harness used by GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase.
  • Terminus 2: The harness used for Terminal-Bench v2.1 within the Intelligence Index.
  • τ-Bench: The harness utilized for τ³-Banking evaluations.

💡 Why it matters

The model’s computer use capability allows it to operate software on a local machine, which is demonstrated through intuitive graphical tasks. Notable examples of this performance include:

  • Modeling and rendering a 3D version of New York City in Blender.
  • Conducting virtual open house tours.
  • Using the mouse cursor to interact with a browser version of MS Paint to redraw images (demonstrated using Astra Medium and High variants).

While traditional LLM strengths include text-based tasks like writing and API usage, Astra’s ability to navigate graphical user interfaces represents a maturing frontier in model capabilities.

#OpenAI #GPT6 #Astra #AIagents #ComputerUse

Source: GPT-6 Astra, Looped Transformers, and Hidden Reasoning
